html:
Austrian doctor, born in 1856 in a small town in Moravia, who founded psychoanalysis and changed how people think about the mind.

He grew up in Vienna in a Jewish family, trained as a neurologist and worked with patients whose troubles had no clear physical cause. He came to believe that much of mental life is unconscious: hidden wishes and memories, often from childhood and often sexual, shape what we feel and do. His method was to let patients talk freely and to interpret their dreams, slips of the tongue and associations.

His book The Interpretation of Dreams came out at the end of 1899. Ideas such as the ego, repression and the Oedipus complex followed. Carl Jung and others later broke away.

Many of his theories are now disputed or rejected by scientists, but the "talking cure" shaped modern therapy, and his ideas spread through art, literature and everyday speech. When Nazi Germany took over Austria in 1938, Freud fled to London, where he died in 1939. Four of his sisters were later murdered in the Holocaust.
